title: Vanishing higher-moment coefficient tail
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\mathrm{law}$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and let $r,j$ be natural numbers. The higher even-moment coefficient tail evaluated at $t=1/(m+1)$ tends to $0$ as the natural number $m$ tends to infinity.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathrm{law}$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
